classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the cream volume stays constant while the total volume changes, then recover the new whole from its percentage.

content.prompt: A dairy farmer found that the milk supplied by his cows was 5% cream and 95% skimmed milk. He wanted to know how much skimmed milk he should add to a litre of milk to reduce the percentage of cream to 4%. (Recall: $1\text{ L}=1000\text{ mL}$.) What is the answer?

answer.short:
250 mL of skimmed milk.

The cream volume stays unchanged; use it as 4% of the final mixture.
answer.worked:
Adding skimmed milk does not change the volume of cream.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Volume of cream}&=\frac{5}{100}\times1000\text{ mL}\\\text{Volume of cream}&=50\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$

In the final mixture, 4% corresponds to 50 mL.

$$\begin{align*}1\%\text{ of the final volume}&=\frac{50}{4}\text{ mL}\\1\%\text{ of the final volume}&=12.5\text{ mL}\\100\%\text{ of the final volume}&=100\times12.5\text{ mL}\\100\%\text{ of the final volume}&=1250\text{ mL}\\\text{Skimmed milk added}&=1250-1000\text{ mL}\\\text{Skimmed milk added}&=250\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
